title: 100 km2, headwater Mesh, Outlet 27, floor 340 m, river target 200 m
deck: Controlled outlet-27 comparison where river refinement still targets 200 m, but the global mesh floor stays at 340 m and therefore clips the local river field.
summary: This case keeps the same outlet, the same river input, the same geology interfaces, and the same river refinement target as the paired 200 m-floor run. The only intended change is the global `min_size`, kept here at 340 m, so the gallery can show why a river target of 200 m does not become visible when the global mesh floor remains higher than the requested local size.
what_it_shows: How the same river network can still look weakly discretized when `interface_size = 200 m` but `min_size = 340 m`.
Why the apparent lack of river refinement comes from a clipped size field, not from missing river constraints.
How much mesh density remains available around outlet 27 when the global floor is kept above the river target.
case_setup: Same input linework as the paired comparison case: 48 river lines, 95 active geology-interface lines.
River refinement request kept at `interface_size = 200 m` over `interface_distance = 610 m`.
Global floor kept at `min_size = 340 m`, so the local river field cannot go below 340 m.

key_parameters: The comparison is controlled: the river target stays at `200 m` in both cases, and the river linework count stays at `48` input lines and `473` embedded river curves.
Here the global floor stays at `min_size = 340 m`, while the river family field still asks for `interface_size = 200 m`.
Because the global floor is higher than the local target, Gmsh cannot realize the requested `200 m` corridor along the rivers.
how_to_read: Use this page together with the paired `floor 200 m, target 200 m` case; the river network and geology are intentionally the same, so the visible difference comes from the global size floor only.
If a river branch still looks under-discretized here, interpret it first as a size-floor effect, not as evidence that the river was dropped from the constraints.
Compare the metrics with the paired case: this run reaches fewer nodes and cells because the 340 m floor prevents part of the local river refinement from appearing.
next_steps: Open :doc:`the paired 200 m-floor case </capability_gallery/cases/mesh_headwater_100km2_outlet_27_geology_rivers_buffer30_floor200_target200>` to see the same outlet once the global floor no longer clips the river target.
